name: beyond_create_processors
description: For api_server use at most one endpoint per processor (one Swagger/OpenAPI operation); Spring Controller classes may have multiple endpoints. Use endpoints or other_info.endpoints. Explicit endpoints takes precedence over nested endpoints and legacy method/path. On update omission preserves, a list replaces, [] empties and null clears routing. Storage is only other_info.endpoints; legacy method/path inputs are converted. Before architecture writes, read the model_storage_design_guide and acceptable_processors returned by model creation/retrieval. Use verified source, configuration, specifications or explicit user requirements; never guess missing classes, routes, framework or subtype. Omit unknown optional values and ask for required information. Read the selected type use_lookup policy: false rejects lookup_attributes and directs automatic SQL targets to OUTPUT. Controller endpoints with verified handlers automatically create handler-named INPUT/OUTPUT Object containers. Read returned contract IDs and auto_created_attributes before adding confirmed child fields. Automatic handler contracts apply to registered handler types including spring_boot_controller and fastapi_endpoint_handler; read controller_endpoint_contract_guide for the complete list. They do not apply to every module or API Server. See controller_endpoint_contract_guide for examples. Large responses use paged delivery even when the operation partially or fully failed. In a paged response outer success is page-delivery status only; inspect data.operation_status.success/is_error, failed_count and bounded failed_preview immediately. Retrieve and assemble ALL page_content fragments to obtain complete created objects, ID mappings and failed entries. Retry only failed items, never the entire partially successful batch. module_name is the physical name and must be unique within the model physical-name namespace. Duplicate creation returns failed[].error_code=MODULE_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS, existing_entity_id, module_name and suggestion. Reuse an existing class/module across roles; package metadata does not enable duplicate names. For pii_data_type and integer encryption_level, read beyond_get_usage_guide(workflow="attribute_security") or beyond_get_definitions(definition_names=["attribute_security_guide"]). Read only the selected model_design_guide:<model_storage_type> and processor_design_guide:<processor_storage_type> for responsibilities, IO policy and data types.

lookup_attributes.description: Internal processor variables for intermediate fetched data and multi-step mappings. Use LOOKUP when a transformation needs temporary values that connect one step to another, such as Entity -> LOOKUP -> OUTPUT.

processor_attribute_create.description: Create payload schema for processor attributes used in beyond_create_processors. Exposes data_type while supporting processor port metadata without requiring persisted-row fields like io_type. In INPUT/OUTPUT/LOOKUP arrays, the array itself defines the role. LOOKUP attributes act like internal module variables for intermediate fetched data and multi-step mappings.

column_name.description: Physical or logical port field name

data_type.description: Use allowed_data_types from processor_storage_types for this storage type. Spring: List<T> for lists (nested_data_type for element type), Number for Double/Float semantics, float[] with data_length for verified vector dimensions. Do not invent new data types.

is_query_parameter.description: For api_server processors - indicates if this attribute is a query parameter. This info can be used for code generation. This data will be added automatically to other_info.

is_path_parameter.description: For api_server processors - indicates if this attribute is a path parameter. This info can be used for code generation. This data will be added automatically to other_info.

is_header.description: For api_server processors - indicates if this attribute is a header. This info can be used for code generation. This data will be added automatically to other_info.

is_session_data.description: For api_server processors - indicates if this attribute is session data. This info can be used for code generation. This data will be added automatically to other_info.

is_body.description: For api_server processors - indicates if this attribute is part of the body. This info can be used for code generation. This data will be added automatically to other_info.

query_with_attribute_ids.description: For lookup attributes - list of input attribute names to be used in the lookup query. This info can be used for code generation. This data will be added automatically to other_info.

transformation_rule.description: For lookup/output attributes - transformation or mapping rule. This info can be used for code generation. This data will be added automatically to other_info.

encryption_level.description: Integer levelNumber: 0=NONE (None), 1=MASKED (Masked), 2=ENCRYPTED (Encrypted), 3=HASHED (Hashed; one-way hash), 4=KEYSERVER (Key Server; encryption key managed by a key server). Writes do not accept null; omission preserves the value on modification.

sensitivity_level.description: Custom sensitivity level defined by the organization. 0 = not specified, 1 = public, 2 = internal, 3 = confidential, 4 = restricted

confidentiality.description: TARA confidentiality classification. L = Low, M = Medium, H = High, S = Safety Critical.

integrity.description: TARA integrity classification. L = Low, M = Medium, H = High, S = Safety Critical.

availability.description: TARA availability classification. L = Low, M = Medium, H = High, S = Safety Critical.

upper_attribute_name.description: Parent attribute name for nested structures (MongoDB, Elasticsearch, JSON, etc.). Null for root-level attributes.

nested_data_type.description: Processor list/array element physical type from this storage type catalog, e.g. Object or String. Accepted on create/add/modify and returned on reads. nested_physical_data_type is an equivalent compatibility alias; if both are supplied they must agree. Null clears the element type.

display_order.description: Display order of the attribute in listings

other_info.description: Additional information about the attribute as json. Put any properties to express this attribute or to generate code for this attribute.

nested_physical_data_type.description: Compatibility alias for nested_data_type; same physical element type and null-clearing semantics.

pii_data_type.description: PII_DATA_TYPE enum name stored verbatim, e.g. DRIVER_LICENSE. Null clears the classification; this is independent of pii_level.

processor_info_create.description: For api_server use at most one endpoint per processor (one Swagger/OpenAPI operation); Spring Controller classes may have multiple endpoints. Use endpoints or other_info.endpoints. Explicit endpoints takes precedence over nested endpoints and legacy method/path. On update omission preserves, a list replaces, [] empties and null clears routing. Storage is only other_info.endpoints; legacy method/path inputs are converted.

processor_name.description: Logical/business processor name. For api_server processors, this is the user-facing API name. Do not use HTTP method/path or code identifiers here.

module_name.description: Physical/code identifier. For every class-backed processor in a Spring Boot Application model, use the simple class name without package (OrderController), including processor_general. Keep verified package_name, qualified_class_name and source_file in other_info for tracing. module_name must be unique within the model physical-name namespace; package metadata does not bypass this. Reuse one class/module across roles rather than creating duplicates. Do not use a route, HTTP verb or method name as the Controller class name. For api_server use the verified single-operation identifier (operationId, controller method or function), never a server/router grouping.

other_info.description: Optional verified source and processor-specific metadata. Controller/API routing is stored in other_info.endpoints; explicit endpoints input takes precedence over nested endpoints and legacy method/path. Filter matchers, Interceptor include/exclude paths and Controller Advice scope are not HTTP endpoints. Omit unknown values.

package_name.description: Verified source package, without the class name. Omit if unknown.

qualified_class_name.description: Verified fully qualified class name for source tracing; module_name remains the simple class name.

source_file.description: Verified source file path. Never fabricate a path from a class name.

matchers.description: Filter applicability conditions, not endpoints. Use only verified matchers.

order.description: Verified Filter or Interceptor execution order.

controller_scope.description: Verified Controller Advice applicability, preserving source selector meaning. Omit unknown scope.

exception_types.description: Verified exception types handled by Controller Advice.

endpoints.description: Verified inbound HTTP routes for a Controller class or API Server boundary. One Controller processor can contain multiple path/method/handler combinations. Omit unknown fields; never assume GET or derive routes from class names. On update omission preserves, an array replaces, [] empties, null clears. Do not use for Filter/Interceptor matching or Advice scope. Stored only in other_info.endpoints; the top-level response is a projection, not a separate stored value. API Server represents one Swagger/OpenAPI operation: endpoints is an array with at most one method/path pair. Different methods or paths require separate processors. Spring Controller classes may have multiple endpoints. Endpoint cardinality follows the storage catalog: is_module=true permits multiple endpoints; false, null or omitted permits at most one. Clients cannot override this flag. This applies to all processor types and both endpoints and other_info.endpoints. Check acceptable_processors or processor_storage_types before writing. Legacy JSON strings encoding an array or null are also accepted, decoded and validated; new writes store arrays or null and top-level endpoints read projections use arrays or null. Existing raw other_info may retain legacy strings until updated. New clients must send arrays. Invalid strings are rejected without clearing metadata.

path.description: Verified request mapping path; resolve class and handler mappings only from evidence.

method.description: Verified HTTP method; omit if unspecified or unknown. Never default to GET.

handler.description: Actual source handler method name without class/package prefix; omit if unknown.

endpoint_id.description: Server-assigned stable Controller endpoint ID. Preserve on edits to retain the contract association.

input_attribute_id.description: Server-managed Controller INPUT Object ID. Preserve on edits; do not invent. Same-handler routes share this ID.

output_attribute_id.description: Server-managed Controller OUTPUT Object ID. Preserve on edits; do not invent. Add verified child fields under this Object.

exposure_level.description: TARA exposure level. 0 = Not defined/follow model exposure level, 1 = Isolated, 2 = Internal, 3 = Partner, 4 = External, 5 = Public. Omit this or set 0 when the processor should follow the model exposure level; set it only when the processor exposure differs from the model.

processor_storage_type.description: Registered processor type ID. The parent model must also allow it. Query beyond_get_definitions(definition_names=["processor_storage_types"]) for IDs, titles and allowed models.
